## When the prices are a guess, the dashboard says so

A new binary sensor, **Published prices missing**, carries Home Assistant's
`problem` device class: red "Problem" in the UI, and usable in an automation
as plainly as `state: "on"`.

It is on when the price for the slot running **right now** is a forecast
instead of a published day-ahead price. Narrow on purpose. Beyond the
published window the series is always a forecast - that is what this
integration is for - and a flag reporting *that* would be on every afternoon
and worth nothing. The current hour was settled at auction yesterday, so a
forecast covering it means the published prices never arrived.

Not hypothetical: on 9 and 10 October the Dutch, Greek, Romanian and Slovak
day-ahead results were missing from both upstream platforms for a day and a
half. Installations in those markets were served a complete series the whole
time, all of it estimated, with nothing to say so.

Two attributes say what the flag rests on: `price_source` (`day_ahead`,
`early_auction` or `forecast` for the current slot) and `published_until`,
the end of the last published slot in your series. An early-auction price
does not raise the flag - it is not the official price either, but it is a
traded one, and against the Dutch result for 10 October it sat 0.94 ct/kWh
away where the model forecast sat 3.18 ct away.

It is not a repair notice, because there is nothing you can fix at your end,
and the entities stay available: the numbers are there, they are only
estimates, and an automation that stops dead helps nobody. What an automation
that spends money can usefully do is widen its margin or wait, rather than
optimise to a third of a cent on a guess. How long the flag has been on is
the entity's own `last_changed`.

## The dashboard card shows it

The card in the README carries it in two places. A badge at the top of the
view shows the flag itself, so you can see the state whichever card you are
looking at. And the price tile has one line that is always there: a green
check with "Official prices until 22:00" while your prices are published, and
a warning in its place, directly above the number, when they are not.

Copy the card again to pick both up.

## Updating from 1.14.x

Nothing to configure. The sensor appears by itself and is off on a normal
day. If it is on right after the update, it is telling the truth: your
market's published prices are missing at that moment.
